import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Standardize column names for easier access
df.columns = df.columns.str.replace(' ', '_').str.lower()

# Fill NaN values in 'sleep_disorder' with 'None' for clearer categorization
df['sleep_disorder'].fillna('None', inplace=True)

# Select relevant columns for the visualization
metrics_to_plot = ['Sleep_Duration', 'Quality_of_Sleep', 'Physical_Activity_Level', 'Stress_Level']
id_vars = ['person_id', 'gender', 'sleep_disorder']

# Melt the dataframe to a long format for easier plotting with seaborn's facetting capabilities
df_long = pd.melt(df, id_vars=id_vars, value_vars=metrics_to_plot,
                  var_name='Metric', value_name='Value')

# Clean up metric names for titles
df_long['Metric'] = df_long['Metric'].str.replace('_', ' ')

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the theme and a visually appealing color palette
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)
palette = "viridis"

# Create a catplot (Categorical plot) with FacetGrid
# Use a violin plot to show the distribution of data across different categories
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df_long,
    x='sleep_disorder',
    y='Value',
    hue='gender',
    col='Metric',
    kind='violin',
    split=True,        # Split violins for the 'hue' variable
    palette=palette,
    sharey=False,      # Each facet will have its own y-axis scale, which is crucial here
    height=6,
    aspect=0.9,
    order=['None', 'Insomnia', 'Sleep Apnea'] # Define a logical order for the x-axis
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set a comprehensive title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Key Health Metrics by Sleep Disorder and Gender', fontsize=20, y=1.05)

# Improve axis labels and subplot titles
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Disorder", "Metric Value")
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name}", size=14)

# Adjust legend
g.legend.set_title("Gender")
sns.move_legend(g, "upper right", bbox_to_anchor=(.98, .95))

# Add annotations to highlight interesting points, e.g., median stress for Insomnia
# This requires iterating through the axes
for i, ax in enumerate(g.axes.flat):
    # Make y-axis labels more readable
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelrotation=15)
    # Add horizontal grid lines for better readability
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# --- Save the Figure ---
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
